title: Introduce temporal color weave and geometry scale
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Define and implement a complementary token set that pairs a time-aware (temporal) color blending system with a geometry scale that maps spacing, radius, and shadow intensity to typographic scale and interaction velocity. Purpose: reduce visual jank across transitions, improve perceived performance on micro-interactions, and simplify engineering mapping for responsive components (buttons, tables, cards, charts). Scope: token lexicon (primary/secondary/ambient ramps), motion-aware alpha ramps for overlays, four-step geometry scale (compact, regular, cozy, expanded) with consistent radius/spacing/shadow deltas, migration guidance for core components, and a small migration helper library for React/vanilla CSS. Accessibility: target WCAG AA contrast for static states and maintain contrast during common animated overlays. Deliverables: token spec doc, Figma library, export script (JSON tokens), PRD for engineering changes, and acceptance tests for contrast and token usage. Constraints and trade-offs: introducing temporal blending increases token surface complexity (more dynamic tokens) which requires runtime logic in some Private deployments; to keep on-prem footprint small, we will include static fallbacks and a server-side precomputed map where needed.
acceptance_criteria: Token spec published with canonical names and examples (color-weave.primary.* color-weave.ambient.* geometry.scale.{compact,regular,cozy,expanded})
Figma library updated and reviewed by Design Leads
Exported JSON tokens integrate with existing token pipeline and pass schema validation
At least three core components (Button, Table Row, Card) use the new tokens in a feature-flagged rollout
Automated contrast checks pass for all static states and the most common animated overlay states
Migration guide and small helper library published in the repo with unit tests
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize token names and examples; produce Figma variants for the four geometry scales
Week 2: Export tokens; implement feature-flagged component variants in the component library (react) for Button and Card
Week 3: Run accessibility checks, iterate on color ramp deltas; add Table row variant
Week 4: Canary rollout to internal apps, gather metrics on perceived latency for micro-interactions
Week 5: Gradual rollout and deprecation of legacy tokens with migration notes
migration_steps: Add feature flag (design.tokens.temporal) to enable new tokens per-app
Install token JSON from design-assets and run token-validate script
Swap token references in component styles (start with Button primary/secondary) and run snapshot tests
Enable canary in staging; monitor visual regressions and accessibility test results
Schedule deprecation PR for legacy tokens after two successful release cycles
notes: Decision: use a 3-layer color model — base ramp / ambient overlay ramp / motion alpha ramp — to enable expressive overlays without breaking base contrast
Trade-off: motion alpha requires runtime composition for some browsers; we will provide pre-composited tokens for low-capability runtimes
Suggest pairing geometry.scale with existing type tokens so developers can choose canonical sizes per breakpoint
